content.user_title: Audit Your B2B Cold Email Program
content.value_statement: Weak outbound results can originate from infrastructure, targeting, messaging, or operations. This workflow organizes evidence and, with its referenced rubric, ranks improvements in a 90-day plan.
actual_capabilities: Collect infrastructure, targeting, messaging, and operations context through one structured intake.
Define 30 available points across infrastructure, targeting, messaging, and operations.
Normalize rubric-based point totals to a 0-100 score and assign an overall letter grade.
Rank three improvement priorities using compounding impact, effort, and sequencing.
Structure a 90-day improvement plan with owners and verification metrics.
Provide a concise report format with optional point-by-point detail.
limitations: The required scoring rubric and underlying framework are not included in the reviewed package; exact point-level scoring requires those references.
Assessment relies on supplied answers; the file defines no automated DNS checks, mailbox tests, or campaign data integrations.
The skill is marked as not directly user-invocable and expects activation through the parent cold-email skill.
Recommendations do not send emails, apply configuration changes, guarantee results, or establish legal compliance.

use_cases.title: Prioritize outbound improvements
use_cases.description: Review a startup outbound program and identify three practical priorities before increasing campaign spending.

use_cases.title: Assess a client program
use_cases.description: Gather client intake answers and prepare an evidence-based review with a phased improvement plan.

use_cases.title: Review operational readiness
use_cases.description: Assess reply handling, booking, sales handoffs, and reporting alongside targeting and messaging.

prompt_templates.title: Start an outbound audit
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit our B2B cold email program. Ask for infrastructure, targeting, messaging, and operations context in one intake message before scoring.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: gather the evidence needed for a review.

prompt_templates.title: Review supplied intake answers
prompt_templates.prompt: Review these intake answers: [answers]. Identify missing evidence and unavailable references before assigning any scores.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: check whether the assessment has enough information.

prompt_templates.title: Score and prioritize improvements
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this audit rubric: [rubric] and these program details: [details]. Score each point and dimension, normalize the total, and rank three improvements.
prompt_templates.scenario: Experienced: complete scoring with the required rubric supplied.

prompt_templates.title: Build an accountable improvement plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this completed audit: [audit] and these constraints: [constraints]. Assign owners and verification metrics across days 1-14, 15-45, and 46-90.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: translate reviewed findings into a staged operational plan.

output_examples.input: We have not documented our sending setup, and our reply process is unclear. Start an outbound audit.
output: Infrastructure: share sending domains, provider, warm-up history, daily limits, and SPF, DKIM, and DMARC status.
Targeting: share your ideal customer definition, pain signals, list source, list size, send volume, and baseline response rate.
Messaging: share your opener, subject lines, sequence cadence, and personalization approach.
Operations: identify reply ownership, response targets, booking process, sales handoff, and reporting cadence.
Scoring remains pending until your answers and the required rubric are available.

output_examples.input: Our completed rubric gives infrastructure 4/8, targeting 6/8, messaging 5/8, and operations 3/6. Authentication, segmentation, and reply ownership need work.
output: Overall score: 60/100, grade C, from 18 earned points out of 30.
Top priorities: resolve authentication gaps, improve segmentation, and assign reply ownership.
Days 1-14: infrastructure owner resolves authentication gaps; verify the configured records.
Days 15-45: campaign owner improves segmentation; compare response rates against the baseline.
Days 46-90: sales operations owner establishes reply ownership; track response time against the agreed target.

best_practices: Supply complete intake answers and the actual scoring rubric before requesting a numeric grade.
Share aggregate metrics and sanitized email samples instead of credentials or unnecessary personal data.
Prioritize infrastructure fixes and give each improvement an owner and a measurable verification target.
anti_patterns: Inventing missing rubric criteria or treating unanswered questions as verified evidence.
Scaling send volume before resolving known infrastructure and deliverability problems.
Treating an audit score as proof of legal compliance or guaranteed campaign performance.

faq.question: Which tools are supported?
faq.answer: The report lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code. The skill source expects activation through the parent cold-email skill.

faq.question: What does the audit cover?
faq.answer: It covers infrastructure, targeting, messaging, and operations, with 8, 8, 8, and 6 available points respectively.

faq.question: How is the overall score calculated?
faq.answer: Divide earned points by 30 and multiply by 100. Individual rubric points receive 0, 0.5, or 1.

faq.question: Is the complete scoring rubric included?
faq.answer: No. The reviewed package contains only SKILL.md and references a separate rubric and framework that must be supplied.

faq.question: Does it test DNS settings or send emails?
faq.answer: No automated tests or sending actions are defined. The workflow evaluates supplied context and produces recommendations.

faq.question: What does the final report contain?
faq.answer: It contains an overall score, dimension results, three ranked priorities, and a 90-day plan. Point-by-point detail is optional.
